LAFC parts ways with head coach Marc Dos Santos

Caleb PongratzSeptember 27, 2026
Spotrac
Share
mls los angeles fc marc dos santos
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:23
Instaread

Los Angeles FC has relieved head coach Marc Dos Santos of his duties, effective immediately, President of Soccer Operations John Thorrington announced.

“Marc has given a great deal to this club over the years, and we are grateful for his commitment, care, and contributions to LAFC,” Thorrington said. “We wish Marc and his family all the best moving forward.”

Dos Santos, 49, joined LAFC as an assistant coach ahead of the 2022 season and took over as head coach in December 2025 following Steve Cherundolo’s departure.

The change comes with LAFC sixth in the Western Conference on 41 points and six regular-season matches remaining. The club has won just one of its last 10 MLS matches. 

Dos Santos finishes his tenure as head coach with a 19-10-10 record across all competitions.

LAFC is now the eighth MLS club to change head coaches this season. 

Orlando City SC mutually parted ways with Oscar Pareja in March. Javier Mascherano stepped down at Inter Miami CF in April, the same month CF Montréal relieved Marco Donadel of his duties. In May, Columbus Crew parted ways with Henrik Rydström, Austin FC dismissed Nico Estévez, Portland Timbers relieved Phil Neville of his duties, and Philadelphia Union mutually parted ways with Bradley Carnell.

LAFC said it will announce its interim coaching plans soon as it begins its search for a new head coach.
